subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How is profit calculated?
questions.explain: Profit = total revenue - total costs.

questions.q: A statement of comprehensive income (profit and loss account) mainly shows a business's:
options: Revenues, costs and profit over a period of time
questions.explain: The profit and loss account (income statement) records revenues, costs and the profit made over a period.

questions.q: Net profit margin is calculated as:
questions.explain: Net profit margin = (net profit divided by revenue) x 100, expressed as a percentage.

questions.q: A business has revenue of 200,000 pounds and gross profit of 80,000 pounds. Its gross profit margin is:
questions.explain: Gross profit margin = (gross profit / revenue) x 100 = (80,000 / 200,000) x 100 = 40%.

questions.q: The average rate of return (ARR) helps a business to:
options: Work out the total fixed costs
Compare the annual profit of an investment against its cost as a percentage
questions.explain: ARR expresses the average yearly profit of an investment as a percentage of the initial cost, aiding investment decisions.

questions.q: Crowdfunding as a source of finance means:
options: Raising small amounts of money from a large number of people, often online
Selling shares on the stock exchange
questions.explain: Crowdfunding raises finance from many people contributing small amounts, usually via an online platform.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an internal source of finance?
questions.explain: Retained profit is generated within the business, making it an internal source of finance.

questions.q: Why can a profitable business still run out of cash?
options: Customers may pay later while the business must pay its own bills now
Profit and cash are the same thing
Profit is always paid in cash immediately
questions.explain: Profit and cash differ in timing; a firm can be profitable yet short of cash if money comes in slowly.

questions.q: Leasing equipment rather than buying it means the business:
options: Pays regular amounts to use the equipment without owning it
Sells the equipment to raise cash
Receives a grant from the government
questions.explain: Leasing lets a business pay to use equipment over time without paying the full purchase cost upfront or owning it.

questions.q: Selling shares (share capital) is generally considered:
options: Always available to a sole trader
A way of borrowing that must be repaid with interest
A long-term external source of finance
questions.explain: Share capital comes from outside the business and does not have to be repaid, making it a long-term external source.

questions.q: Retained profit is a popular source of finance for established businesses because it:
options: Can only be used by plcs
Must be paid back within 30 days
Has no interest cost and does not have to be repaid
questions.explain: Retained profit is internal, carries no interest and does not need repaying, making it a low-cost source of finance.

questions.q: The margin of safety is:
options: The total amount of fixed costs
The difference between actual sales and the break-even level of sales
questions.explain: Margin of safety is how far actual (or planned) sales exceed the break-even output.

questions.q: Which item would appear as a cash inflow on a cash-flow forecast?
questions.explain: Cash received from sales is money coming into the business, so it is an inflow on a cash-flow forecast.

questions.q: Gross profit is calculated as:
options: Revenue minus all expenses and tax
questions.explain: Gross profit = revenue - cost of sales (the direct cost of making the goods sold).

questions.q: Variable costs are costs that:
options: Stay the same whatever the output
Change directly with the level of output
Are paid only once a year
questions.explain: Variable costs (e.g. raw materials) rise and fall with the amount produced.

questions.q: If selling price is 10 pounds and variable cost per unit is 6 pounds, the contribution per unit is:
questions.explain: Contribution per unit = selling price (10) - variable cost per unit (6) = 4 pounds.

questions.q: A bank overdraft is best described as a source of finance that is:
options: A long-term loan repaid over 25 years
A grant that never has to be repaid
A short-term facility allowing a business to spend more than is in its account
questions.explain: An overdraft lets a business withdraw more than its account balance for the short term, usually to cover small cash shortfalls.

questions.q: On a break-even chart, the break-even point is shown where:
options: The total revenue line crosses the total costs line
The revenue line reaches its highest point
questions.explain: Break-even occurs where the total revenue line crosses the total costs line, so revenue exactly covers costs.

questions.q: Which of these is a fixed cost?
questions.explain: Rent does not change with output, so it is a fixed cost.

questions.q: Which of these is a long-term source of external finance?
options: A mortgage repaid over many years
questions.explain: A mortgage is repaid over many years, making it a long-term external source of finance.

questions.q: Share capital as a source of finance is raised by:
options: Borrowing from a bank over 12 months
Selling shares in the company to investors
questions.explain: Share capital is money raised by selling shares to investors, who become part-owners of the company.

questions.q: A cash-flow forecast is used to:
options: Predict future cash coming in and going out
questions.explain: A cash-flow forecast predicts the timing of cash inflows and outflows to spot shortages early.
